data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Plus has new wireless firmware that can support up to 7GHz of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone 14 Plus. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning.

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most commonly reported iPhone 14 Plus Wi-Fi issues are…

Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 14 Plus

Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver

Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi

High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections

iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi

iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 14 Plus are pretty common issues found on other wireless-supported devices too! It also does not necessarily indicate that there is anything specifically wrong with your iPhone 14 Plus wireless hardware. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issue has been resolved

Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again

Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection

Restore the default network connection

(Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

Update your iOS to the latest version available

If none of the solutions mentioned above work to resolve your Wi-Fi issue on your iPhone 14 Plus, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 14 Plus offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update. This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 14 Plus

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 14 Plus power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician. data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
The iPhone 14 Plus is one of the best phones on the market, considering its audio output quality. It has a dual stereo speaker with noise cancelation and spatial audio features. It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. Should keep in mind that, the left speaker grill is not a speaker but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio only comes out of the right speaker grill and is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone 14 Plus are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when on calls. However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone 14 Plus users are:

No sound on audio playback

No sound on voice calls

Distorted/Low sound on the speakers

Headphones not working

Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.

Phone stuck in Headphone mode

Ringer Switch not working/ Audio level increases or decreases automatically/ Physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “Do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. They are:

Check the ringer switch to see if it is in sound mode

Restarting Your Phone

Disabling your Bluetooth on the iPhone 14 Plus

Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode

Check the sound notification settings and try turning noise cancelation off.

Try using headphones and check if the sounds come okay in headphones.

Try removing any protective cases

Clean speaker grills for dirt and debris

if none of the fixes work for your phone, you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones. data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the IPSW files from iTunes from a PC. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen on iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

To check if your iPhone is updated

If the update still fails try updating it from another pc

To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)

Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.

Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info page with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions. However, not all problems can be fixed only by DIY fixes. Some errors might require some handy work around the inner parts of the phone which should be done by a professional iPhone technician.

data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone 14 Plus comes with upgraded network connectivity compared to previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite technological advancements from previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 14 Plus network connectivity. Such as loss of the network, prompt disconnections, and inability to find or locate the network. The most common issues, however, are often discussed on Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding networks in iPhone 14 Plus are:

Network never reaches the full level

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

iPhone 14 Plus gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

These common issues, however, can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 14 Plus. To resolve this, Apple recommends its iPhone 14 Plus users some DIY (do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. -requires a restart of the device

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set it up, go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network.

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to be checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues with your iPhone 14 Plus. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.description:
The new iPhone comes with an almost 4323 mAh battery. The battery is optimized perfectly for the phone. However, it may be for some manufacturer error or something about some faulty app optimization, you may not get the smoothest output from your iPhone 14 Plus battery. Most users have reported that the iPhone’s battery starts draining after the system has updated to iOS 14 Plus Several other issues may cause battery drain issues also. These issues include:

The battery of the iPhone 14 Plus runs out too quickly after the update

The battery of the iPhone 14 Plus runs out after installing an app/ update an app

The battery of the iPhone drains quickly after turning on the optimized charging mode

The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly

These are the most common problems regarding battery draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

Turn off background iCloud/iTunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount

When not in use turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service in your iPhone

Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 14 Plus. It may reduce battery health

Turn on optimized battery charging to save your battery life and protect it from draining

Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 14 Plus to auto-brightness

Turn off Background app refresh From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh

Try running it on low power mode from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON

Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery-draining issues, it may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. Make sure your touchscreen protector doesn’t interfere with the proper operation

Disconnect your USB-lightning port to check if it works

If your phone is above normal temperature, wait for it to cool down and then try again

Restart your device

data.title: Boot Loop
data.description:
The iPhone 14 Plus offers the users a new iOS version (iOS 13 upgradable to iOS 14) and updates it forward. Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the Boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the Apple logo. Then goes black and again shows only the apple logo on the screen, the phone can show nothing beyond that.

This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update happens on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop such as:

Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)

The battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.

Hardware Damage.

Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

Force Restart Your iPhone 14 Plus

(press the volume up button (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the apple logo)

Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.

data.description:

The phone's display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)

Connect the lightning cable and charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

data.description:
However, after using the phone for a long time or by accident; your charging dock of the phone may get faulty or damaged, and you might need to get it replaced. The most common issues with the iPhone 14 Plus charging dock are:

  • The battery charges very slowly
  • iPhone 14 Plus is not charging beyond 80%
  • Charging Not available or Liquid has been detected in the charging port error
  • The charging dock can’t be connected to a USB-supported device through a lightning cable

If your phone has any one of these issues or something not mentioned in the list of common issues. You will still like to check out these DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may solve the problem regarding the charging dock in your iPhone 14 Plus.

  • Make sure you don’t have any debris or dirt on your charging dock. This may prevent charging
  • Make sure your power outlet isn’t faulty
  • If your phone is wet, wait until it is dry to charge your phone

data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth

You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.

Never charge your phone until you have made sure it is completely dry

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. What are the common iPhone 14 Plus problems we fix?

Battery degrading after sustained daily use

Despite having the largest battery in the standard iPhone 14 lineup, the iPhone 14 Plus battery does degrade over time. Three years of daily charging cycles, particularly in Bangladesh's heat, reduce cell capacity. Battery replacement restores the excellent all-day battery life this model is known for. iPhone 14 Plus battery replacement

Cracked large 6.7-inch OLED display

The 6.7-inch Super Retina XDR OLED is the main reason most people choose the 14 Plus over the standard 14. Cracking or OLED damage destroys the large-screen experience. We replace the full assembly — OLED panel, digitiser, and bracket — and confirm the full touch surface is responsive after repair. iPhone 14 Plus screen replacement

Lightning port not charging consistently

Lint and pocket debris in the Lightning port cause most charging failures on the iPhone 14 Plus. We clean during every free diagnosis — port flex replacement only when cable damage is confirmed. iPhone 14 Plus charging issues

Rear camera blur or autofocus failing

The dual-camera system on the iPhone 14 Plus — wide and ultrawide — can develop blur and autofocus failure after drops that impact the rear glass and camera bump. iPhone 14 Plus camera repair

Face ID not working after drop or prior repair

TrueDepth sensors above the display notch control Face ID. Physical impact or a poorly executed prior screen repair can break sensor pairing and disable Face ID. iPhone 14 Plus Face ID repair

data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
This correlation between the power button and the battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhones. These power issues include:

Phone does not turn on

The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem

iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.

iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.

Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc.

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone 14 Plus. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do It Yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help with the issue on your device. Such as...

Force restart your iPhone ( Press Volume up (+) and quickly press volume down (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process)

Check your Lightning cable and adapter to see if they are functioning properly

Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 14 Plus charging porthole

Limit background processes by stopping background app refresh

Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off

Sometimes excessive battery drain can happen due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version. If none of these methods work to resolve the issue on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians.iFixit bd is an iPhone servicing center located around 4 different service points around Dhaka, Bangladesh. We provide the best iPhone servicing support in Bangladesh.
